The background is RANDOMISED per shortcut from the six tile colours — the same palette the dashboard tiles use. The colour you get here is the colour the tile and widget will be.

Use the swatch tweak above the artboard to see the other five.

Redesigned: this used to be a slot-based "madlib" template that only led somewhere via a "Describe the widget" pill — a screen with no value of its own. Free text is now the primary input right here, quick-add chips cover the fast common cases, and the shortcut's steps build up live below as you add them, turn by turn.

Free text lives behind the "Describe the widget" button, not a separate link. Same coloured ground, so it reads as one flow.

The examples are there because a blank box is the hardest thing to answer.

Manual creation uses the same sentence-with-slots language as the AI builder — the only difference is that YOU pick every slot instead of the model proposing them.

The swatch row sets the shortcut's colour, which is why this screen shows it and the AI one doesn't.
